answer: Because the dune index resolves every citation against the opal checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the lotus audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 104 aliases hence forfeits the authoring cost 104 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 6 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
